Rashi on Sanhedrin 21a:12:1.hebrew: למאן דדריש וי"ו - ר"ע בד' מיתות ב"ד (לקמן סנהדרין דף נא.): ישמעאל אחי, בת ובת אני דורש:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 21a:12:1.english: According to the one who interprets [the letter] vav - [This refers to] Rabbi Akiva in [the chapter entitled] Arba Mitot Beit Din (below, Sanhedrin 51a): “Yishmael, my brother, I interpret [the difference between] bat and u-vat.”

Rashi on Sanhedrin 21a:14:1.english: Plowed with my calf - Samson called his wife [this] when she told them his riddle.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 21a:16:1.hebrew: ואמר רב שקלה מיכל למטרפסה - זה היה פרעון חטאתה, מה שנכתב בצידו: "לא היה לה ולד" — אלמא, מההוא מעשה ואילך לא הוה לה, אבל מקמי הכי איכא למימר דהוה לה:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 21a:16:1.english: And Rav said: Michal received her punishment - This was the retribution for her sin: that which is written alongside it, "she had no child" — evidently, from that incident onward she did not have [any children], but prior to this, it can be said that she did have [a child].

Rashi on Sanhedrin 21a:17:1.english: But isn’t it written: “And David took more” - This implies that he had many wives.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 21a:18:1.hebrew: יפת תואר - הנשבית במלחמה, כדכתיב (דברים כח) וראית בשביה:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 21a:18:1.english: A woman of beautiful form - [A woman] taken captive in war, as it is written (Deuteronomy 21:11): “And you see among the captives.”

Rashi on Sanhedrin 21a:19:1.hebrew: תמר - אחות אבשלום, בת יפת תואר היתה: קודם שנתגיירה בלב שלם מעכה אמו, ילדה לו לדוד את תמר, והיתה אצלו בתורת יפת תואר:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 21a:19:1.english: Tamar - Absalom’s sister was the daughter of a woman of beautiful form: Before Maacah, his mother, converted with a whole heart, she bore Tamar to David, and she was with him under the legal status of a woman of beautiful form.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 21a:19:2.english: “Now, therefore, speak, please,” etc. - Tamar was giving advice to Amnon.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 21a:19:3.hebrew: מי הוה שרייה ליה אלא שמע מינה - עדיין לא נתגיירה אמו כשילדתה. ותנן: ולד שפחה וכותית מישראל אין לו קורבת אב, במסכת יבמות (דף כב.) — מי שיש לו בן מ"מ וכו':
Rashi on Sanhedrin 21a:19:3.english: Would he have permitted her to him? Rather, learn from this - Her mother had not yet converted when she gave birth to her. And we learned: The offspring of a maidservant or a gentile woman from an Israelite has no paternal relationship, in tractate Yevamot (22a) — “One who has a son from any source, etc.”

Rashi on Sanhedrin 21a:1:1.english: And they anointed him - It is written concerning Solomon.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 21a:21:1.english: And feign illness - Make yourself like a sick person.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 21a:23:1.english: That Jewish women did not have - [This was] before they sinned and “the daughters of Zion were haughty” (Isaiah 3:16).

Rashi on Sanhedrin 21a:23:2.english: [Neither] armpit hair - Under the armpits of their arms.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 21a:24:1.hebrew: גדרה תמר - בדמעתה וזעקתה, ונהגה עצמה בבזיון — נשאו שאר נשים ק"ו בעצמן: מה בנות מלכים אירע קלקול זה, בהדיוטות — על אחת כמה וכמה:
Rashi on Sanhedrin 21a:24:1.english: Tamar established a fence - Through her tears and her outcry, and [as] she conducted herself in humiliation, other women drew an a fortiori inference regarding themselves: If this violation occurred to the daughters of kings, to commoners — all the more so!

Rashi on Sanhedrin 21a:2:1.english: And it shall be for Aaron and his sons - It is written concerning the shewbread.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 21a:3:1.english: Eighteen - [This] is derived for us below.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 21a:5:1.english: A wealthy [widow], one may take collateral from her - Because she does not need that garment, [such that one would have] to return it to her at night.

Rashi on Sanhedrin 21a:5:2.english: [You] give her a bad name - In that she enters your house morning and evening.

Tosafot on Sanhedrin 21a:19:1.hebrew: דאי ס"ד בת נישואין הואי אחתיה מי הוה שרייה ליה - מכאן קשה לפ"ה שפירש בפ"ק דקידושין (דף כב.): "והבאתה אל תוך ביתך" — מלמד שלא ילחצנה במלחמה, פי' שלא יבא עליה במלחמה. ומשמע מתוך פי' הקונטרס דאפילו ביאה ראשונה אסורה במלחמה עד לאחר כל המעשים כולן, וא"כ לא בא דוד על מעכה רק לאחר שנתגיירה, וא"כ בת נישואין היא, והיכי שריא תמר לאמנון? אחתיה היא! ועוד, דהא אמרינן (שם דף כא.): "דלא דברה תורה אלא כנגד יצר הרע", משמע שבמלחמה ביאה ראשונה הואי. לכך פירש ר"ת התם: שלא ילחצנה במלחמה לבא עליה ביאה שניה. ומחלוקת בירושלמי בין רב ושמואל מן הפי': דרב אמר אינה מותרת במלחמה אלא ביאה ראשונה, ושמואל אמר אף לא ביאה ראשונה ולא ביאה שניה. וזה לשון הירושלמי: "תרתי מילין אתון אמרין משמיה דרב וליתא; הכא אתון אמרין משמיה דרב: אסור לבא עליה ביאה שניה, ואני אומר: לא ביאה ראשונה ולא ביאה שניה". וא"כ קשיא לשמואל הך דהכא, כדפרישית. על כן נראה למימר, דתמר לא היתה בת דוד, שאמה כבר היתה מעוברת כשבאת למלחמה. והא דכתיב (שמואל ב י״ג:י״ח): "כי כן תלבשנה בנות המלכים מעילים" — מתוך שגדלה בחיקו של דוד, קרי לה בת מלך:
Tosafot on Sanhedrin 21a:19:1.english: "And if it enters your mind [to say] she was the daughter of marriage, would his sister have been permitted to him?" - From here there is a difficulty for the explanation of Rashi, who explained in the first chapter of Kiddushin (22a): "'And you shall bring her into your house' — this teaches that he must not pressure her in wartime"; [Rashi] explained: that he must not engage in intercourse with her in wartime. And it is implied by the explanation of the Kuntres [Rashi] that even the first act of intercourse is forbidden in wartime until after all the procedures [for taking a female captive are completed]. And if so, David did not engage in intercourse with Maacah until after she had converted, and if so, she [Tamar] was the daughter of marriage, and how could Tamar be permitted to Amnon? She was his sister! And furthermore, we say (there, 21b): "The Torah only spoke against the evil inclination," which implies that in wartime the first act of intercourse took place. Therefore, Rabbeinu Tam explained there: "that he must not pressure her in wartime" [means] to engage in a second act of intercourse with her. And [there is] a dispute in the Yerushalmi between Rav and Shmuel regarding this interpretation: for Rav said, she is permitted in wartime only for the first act of intercourse; and Shmuel said, neither the first act of intercourse nor the second act of intercourse [is permitted in wartime]. And this is the language of the Yerushalmi: "Two things you say in the name of Rav and they are not [correct]; here you say in the name of Rav: It is forbidden to engage in a second act of intercourse with her, but I say: Neither a first act of intercourse nor a second act of intercourse [is permitted in wartime]." And if so, this [passage] here is difficult for Shmuel, as I explained. Therefore, it seems [proper] to say that Tamar was not David's daughter, for her mother was already pregnant when she arrived at the war. And as for that which is written (II Samuel 13:18): "For with such robes were the king's daughters appareled" — because she grew up in the lap of David [as his ward], [Scripture] calls her a king's daughter.
